title: Global Atlas of Advance Directives, Incapacity Mandates & Cross-Border Portability (2026)

advanceDirectiveDistribution.label: Binding statute with national registry or e-health lookup
advanceDirectiveDistribution.description: Enacted national legislation provides a legally binding advance healthcare directive or living will backed by a dedicated national registry or nationwide electronic health record lookup accessible to treating clinicians.

advanceDirectiveDistribution.label: Binding statute (clinician, notary, or sub-national filing)
advanceDirectiveDistribution.description: Dedicated national, constitutional-court, or state/provincial statutes recognize binding advance healthcare directives and medical proxies, stored with clinicians, civil-law notaries, or sub-national systems rather than one central national database.

advanceDirectiveDistribution.label: Patients' rights written-refusal or medical-council framework
advanceDirectiveDistribution.description: Enacted Patients' Rights, Public Health, or Palliative Care statutes or national medical-council guidelines formally govern written treatment refusals, palliative care goals, and designated hospital spokespersons without a standalone living-will statute.

advanceDirectiveDistribution.label: Contemporaneous clinical consent & family consultation
advanceDirectiveDistribution.description: Medical treatment decisions rely on contemporaneous patient consent while competent and physician-family consultation thereafter, without a dedicated statutory advance-directive or codified advance-refusal regime.

incapacityMandateDistribution.label: Continuing, lasting, or durable Power of Attorney
incapacityMandateDistribution.description: Dedicated statutory enduring, lasting, durable, or future power of attorney survives or activates upon loss of mental capacity (immediately, upon medical certification, or via administrative/notarial registration) without court-appointed guardianship.

incapacityMandateDistribution.label: Notarized voluntary guardianship or CRPD support designation
incapacityMandateDistribution.description: Enacted civil-code or UN CRPD legislation allows a capable adult to execute a notarized voluntary-guardianship contract or preventive support/accompaniment designation that binds or guides supervisory or court activation if capacity declines.

incapacityMandateDistribution.label: Ordinary PoA lapses; court guardianship on incapacity
incapacityMandateDistribution.description: Standard civil or common-law mandates require ongoing capacity and terminate, freeze, or become legally vulnerable upon mental incapacity, requiring judicial guardianship, curatorship, or interdiction proceedings.

caregiverProtectionDistribution.label: Statutory paid caregiver or end-of-life accompaniment leave
caregiverProtectionDistribution.description: National employment or social-insurance legislation provides paid or wage-replaced leave specifically for employed relatives caring for or accompanying a seriously ill or dying family member.

caregiverProtectionDistribution.label: Statutory carer cash allowance or job-protected unpaid leave
caregiverProtectionDistribution.description: Statute provides either a dedicated monthly caregiver/constant-attendance cash supplement or job-protected unpaid family-caregiver / inpatient-companion leave.

caregiverProtectionDistribution.label: Patient sick pay, invalidity pension, or fund withdrawal only
caregiverProtectionDistribution.description: Statutory protection centers on the ill person's own paid sick leave, contributory invalidity pension, or early provident-fund medical withdrawal, while family caregivers rely on annual or employer-agreed leave.

hcch35Distribution.label: HCCH #35 in force nationwide
hcch35Distribution.description: 2000 Hague Protection of Adults Convention is in force nationwide, providing treaty rules on jurisdiction, applicable law, and cross-border recognition of powers of representation granted for incapacity.

hcch35Distribution.label: HCCH #35 in force for Scotland only (UK)
hcch35Distribution.description: United Kingdom ratification extends strictly to Scotland; Continuing and Welfare Powers of Attorney under Scots law fall within HCCH #35, whereas England & Wales LPAs and Northern Ireland EPAs remain outside treaty scope.

hcch35Distribution.label: Acceded Oct 2026 (enters into force 1 Aug 2027)
hcch35Distribution.description: Montenegro deposited its instrument of accession on 13 October 2026; HCCH #35 enters into force for Montenegro on 1 August 2027.

hcch35Distribution.label: Signed HCCH #35 (not yet ratified / not in force)
hcch35Distribution.description: State has signed the 2000 Hague Protection of Adults Convention (Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Poland, Romania) without ratifying; domestic conflict-of-laws rules govern foreign mandates.

hcch35Distribution.label: Non-party to HCCH #35 (domestic recognition rules)
hcch35Distribution.description: Outside the 2000 Hague Protection of Adults Convention; foreign powers of attorney and guardianship orders have no automatic multilateral recognition and typically require local execution or court validation.

apostilleDistribution.label: 1961 Hague Apostille in force (November 2026)
apostilleDistribution.description: Notarized powers of attorney and medical certificates receive single-stamp signature authentication across contracting states (without conferring substantive incapacity recognition).

apostilleDistribution.label: Acceded; enters into force 28 February 2027 (Thailand)
apostilleDistribution.description: Thailand deposited its accession on 30 June 2026; consular legalization applies until entry into force on 28 February 2027.

apostilleDistribution.label: Non-party (diplomatic / consular legalization required)
apostilleDistribution.description: Cross-border powers of attorney and clinical records require multi-step Foreign Ministry and embassy legalization unless bilaterally exempt.

corridorPortabilityDistribution.label: Mutual nationwide HCCH #35 portability
corridorPortabilityDistribution.description: Both corridor states apply the 2000 Hague Protection of Adults Convention nationwide, enabling treaty-backed recognition of incapacity mandates (Article 15) and Central Authority coordination.

corridorPortabilityDistribution.label: Sub-national UK-Scotland HCCH #35 portability only
corridorPortabilityDistribution.description: Partner state applies HCCH #35 nationwide while UK ratification covers Scotland only; England & Wales LPAs and Northern Ireland EPAs require separate local mandates or court steps.

corridorPortabilityDistribution.label: Asymmetric (only one state in HCCH #35)
corridorPortabilityDistribution.description: Only one of the two corridor countries is a Contracting State to HCCH #35, leaving families without a reciprocal treaty bridge and generally requiring parallel local mandates while capacity holds.

corridorPortabilityDistribution.label: Neither state in HCCH #35 (parallel local mandates)
corridorPortabilityDistribution.description: Neither corridor state participates in HCCH #35; cross-border bank accounts, care decisions, and property require separate compliant domestic mandates in each country before capacity declines.

referenceSources.issuer: Hague Conference on Private International Law (HCCH)
referenceSources.scope: Verifies Apostille treaty force across 127 of 196 sovereign countries in November 2026 (plus Thailand's 28 February 2027 entry into force) and across 39 of 40 cross-border serious-illness corridors.

referenceSources.title: Proposal for a Regulation on Jurisdiction, Applicable Law, Recognition and Enforcement of Measures and Cooperation in Matters Relating to the Protection of Adults (COM(2023) 280 final)
referenceSources.scope: European Union legislative package addressing cross-border non-recognition of powers of representation and proposing a European Certificate of Representation alongside coordinated HCCH #35 participation.

referenceSources.title: Recommendation CM/Rec(2009)11 on Principles Concerning Continuing Powers of Attorney and Advance Directives for Incapacity
referenceSources.issuer: Council of Europe Committee of Ministers
referenceSources.scope: International legal benchmark favoring self-determination through continuing mandates and advance directives over judicial deprivation of legal capacity.

referenceSources.title: Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD), Article 12: Equal Recognition Before the Law
referenceSources.scope: Global human-rights standard underpinning supported decision-making and advance support-agreement reforms across Latin America, Europe, and Asia.

referenceSources.title: Directive (EU) 2019/1158 on Work-Life Balance for Parents and Carers (Article 6 Carers' Leave)
referenceSources.issuer: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
referenceSources.scope: Establishes a minimum statutory carers' leave floor across EU Member States alongside national paid palliative and family-caregiver benefit schemes.

referenceSources.title: Palliative Care: Health Systems, Essential Medicines, and Family Support
referenceSources.scope: Global public-health benchmark on integrating advance care planning, pain relief, and family caregiver support into national health systems.

referenceSources.title: Clarvia Global Statutory Source & Reference Dataset for Terminal Illness and Bereavement Administration (592 Guides, 196 Countries & 200 Cross-Border Corridors)
referenceSources.scope: Underlying 592-guide, 5,396-citation dataset from which all 196 domestic terminal-illness guides (1,541 citations) and 40 cross-border serious-illness guides (397 citations) in this atlas are derived.
